In the special case $G=SU(2)$ in its defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$, with $h(v,w)=v^*w$ and $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$, the associated Hermitian bundle $E=P\times_{SU(2)}\mathbb C^2$ has

$$
q_B(P,\omega)=-\langle c_2(E),[X]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,
$$

where $c_2(E)\in H^4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the integral second Chern class and $[X]\in H_4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the orientation fundamental class. This sign is fixed by the library convention $c(E,\nabla)=\det(I-\Omega_\nabla/(2\pi i))$.

For the superconformal index, use Euclidean radial quantization on a unit three-sphere, defined by writing the punctured Euclidean space as $(t,\Omega)=(\log |x|,x/|x|)\in\mathbb R\times S^3$. Let $\mathcal H(S^3)$ be the resulting graded Hilbert space, $E$ its dimensionless radial Hamiltonian, $J_1$ one chosen Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan generator, $F$ fermion parity, and $Q$ the selected supercharge with radial Hilbert adjoint $S=Q^\dagger$. In this normalization the superconformal algebra gives the nonnegative operator

$$\delta=2\{S,Q\}=E-2J_1-\frac32R.$$

Use the convention in which $Q$ is the component whose scalar chiral-primary branch has $d_{\mathcal O}-3r_{\mathcal O}/2$ as its anticommutator eigenvalue. For its conjugate component $\bar Q$ with radial adjoint $\bar S=\bar Q^\dagger$, write $J_2$ for the other Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan; its conjugate anticommutator is $2\{\bar S,\bar Q\}=E-2J_2+3R/2$. On a scalar superconformal primary both Cartan eigenvalues are zero, so these are the two scalar-primary positivity bounds used on this page.

For the index sector require the closed odd operator $D_Q=\sqrt2(Q+S)$ to be self-adjoint with $D_Q^2=\delta$ as a closed composition equality. Require also $\delta=2(SQ+QS)$ as an equality on the full intersection of the two composition domains, not merely as an extension of an identity on test vectors. Supply an orthonormal basis of simultaneous eigenvectors of $\delta,J_1',\ldots,J_k'$ and $(-1)^F$, with real energy/charge labels $(\lambda,\mathbf j)$, parity label $\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$, and maximal diagonal self-adjoint domains. The joint $(\lambda,\mathbf j)$ subspace includes the basis vectors of both parity labels; write $P_{\lambda,\mathbf j}$ for its orthogonal projection. Here $\lambda\ge0$, the joint energy/charge labels form a supplied countable set, and entire gap eigenspaces, including the protected kernel, may be infinite-dimensional. Require $P_{\lambda,\mathbf j}D(T)\subset D(T)$ and $TP_{\lambda,\mathbf j}\psi=P_{\lambda,\mathbf j}T\psi$ for $T=Q,S,D_Q$ on $D(T)$. These combined-parity projections are the reducing projections; parity-specific projections are not required to commute with odd operators. The grading preserves each joint $(\lambda,\mathbf j)$ subspace and anticommutes with the odd operators on their domains. These reducing-domain conditions specify the actual spectral compatibility; common-domain commutators alone are insufficient.

For $\beta>0$ and finite real or complex chemical potentials $\boldsymbol\mu$, define the weighted exponential first on the finite joint-eigenvector span by the eigenvalues $\exp(-\beta\lambda+\sum_a\mu_a j_a)$. Require its closure to be bounded trace class for every $\beta>0$ at the chosen $\boldsymbol\mu$. This is the meaning of the exponential in the index observable, not an unspecified product of unbounded operators. Every joint block then has finite dimension: its weight is nonzero and infinitely many equal singular values would violate trace class. Infinite total gap multiplicities are permitted through infinitely many joint blocks. Define

$$\mathcal I(\beta,\boldsymbol\mu)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H(S^3)}\left((-1)^F\exp\left[-\beta\delta+\sum_{a=1}^k\mu_aJ_a'\right]\right).$$

If the trace is not trace class, the same symbol may be used only for a specified formal series whose coefficients are defined; it does not denote a convergent partition function. The index is called protected against $\beta$-variation when the stated operator and trace hypotheses imply that positive-$\delta$ states cancel in the graded trace, as proved by the index-pair theorem on this page. A source's further claim of invariance under changing a coupling requires its own stated deformation hypotheses. A protected primary here means a named primary whose dimension is fixed by a specified shortening relation; the word alone asserts no deformation invariance.

derivations.claim: For a block $b$ with $\lambda_b>0$, let $K_b=(Q_b+S_b)$. The block-domain and adjoint hypotheses make $K_b$ an everywhere-defined odd self-adjoint finite-dimensional operator. The block nilpotency and the exact anticommutator identity give $K_b^2=Q_bS_b+S_bQ_b=\lambda_b I/2$. Thus $B_b=\sqrt{2/\lambda_b}K_b$ is a unitary odd involution exchanging the two block parity spaces. This uses this page's supercharge normalization, not the differently normalized right-handed charge on the index page.

The restriction $U_b$ commutes with $K_b$. Since $U_b$ is even, $B_b$ intertwines its even and odd restrictions, which are therefore unitarily conjugate and have equal finite traces. The signed contribution from this block, including its common heat factor, is zero. The full weighted operator is trace class by [A1], so its basis diagonal is absolutely summable; regrouping by the countable blocks preserves the sum. Only zero-gap blocks contribute, even if infinitely many blocks share a gap.

For $\psi\in\ker\delta$, the explicit kernel-domain hypothesis puts $\psi$ in $D(QS)\cap D(SQ)$. Since $Q$ is closed and $S=Q^\dagger$, the anticommutator equality gives $0=\langle\psi,\delta\psi\rangle=2(\|Q\psi\|^2+\|S\psi\|^2)$, hence $Q\psi=S\psi=0$. Conversely, a vector in both operator kernels lies in both composition domains because $Q\psi=S\psi=0$; the anticommutator equality then gives $\delta\psi=0$. The restriction of the trace-class heat-weighted operator to this kernel is just $U$, so its signed trace converges absolutely and contains no $\beta$. This proves the stated identity and includes an infinite protected kernel whenever the insertion makes its trace convergent.

A four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ SCFT state-space datum used here consists of a $\mathbb Z_2$-graded complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^{\bar 0}\oplus\mathcal H^{\bar 1}$ with positive inner product, a common invariant dense domain $\mathcal D$, and a representation on $\mathcal D$ of the real Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{psu}(2,2|4)$. For homogeneous matrices its bracket is the graded commutator $[X,Y]_{\mathrm s}=XY-(-1)^{|X||Y|}YX$. This algebra is the quotient by its central real line $\mathbb R\,iI_{4|4}$ of the real form of the supertrace-zero $4|4$ matrix Lie superalgebra preserving a Hermitian form of signature $(2,2)$ on the even block and positive signature on the odd block; for a block-diagonal matrix $A\oplus D$, the supertrace is $\operatorname{tr}A-\operatorname{tr}D$. Its even part is $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(4)_R$, with $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)\cong\mathfrak{so}(4,2)$; its odd generators are the Poincar\'e supercharges $Q,\bar Q$ and the special superconformal charges $S,\bar S$. The conformal generators include translations $P_\mu$, Lorentz transformations $M_{\mu\nu}$, dilations $D$, and special conformal transformations $K_\mu$.

Use radial quantization throughout the representation-theoretic data below. The closures of the generators have Hilbert adjoints $P_\mu^\dagger=K_\mu$, $M_{\mu\nu}^\dagger=M_{\mu\nu}$, and $D^\dagger=D$; the chosen Hermitian generators of the compact $SU(4)_R$ and Lorentz $SU(2)$ subgroups are self-adjoint. The radial Hamiltonian is $E=D$, self-adjoint with spectrum bounded below. Thus translations $P_\mu$ are not asserted to be self-adjoint on the radial Hilbert space. A unitary representation here means that the inner product is positive, the generators have the common invariant dense domain just specified, and the displayed adjoint relations hold as operator equalities. A superconformal primary is a vector annihilated by all $K_\mu$ and all special superconformal charges; its descendants are obtained by applying $P_\mu$ and Poincar\'e supercharges. A scalar superconformal primary is such a nonzero vector that is a simultaneous eigenvector of $D$ and $R$ and transforms trivially under both Lorentz $SU(2)$ factors, so $J_1=J_2=0$. This is only the representation-theoretic data used here; it does not define a local operator algebra or assert a continuum quantum field theory construction.

For the scalar-primary sector, use the selected $\mathcal N=1$ subalgebra and normalize its $U(1)_R$ generator $R$ so that the three adjoint chiral superfields have scalar charge $2/3$. Write $d_{\mathcal O}$ for the eigenvalue of the dilation generator on a scalar superconformal primary $|\mathcal O\rangle$ and $r_{\mathcal O}$ for its $R$ charge. The scalar unitarity bound in this convention is $d_{\mathcal O}\geq 3|r_{\mathcal O}|/2$; equality in the positive-charge branch is the chiral-primary shortening condition. The local conditional norm argument is given by the chiral-primary unitarity item on this page; no classification of all $\mathfrak{psu}(2,2|4)$ representations is asserted here.

For the superconformal index, use Euclidean radial quantization on a unit three-sphere, defined by writing the punctured Euclidean space as $(t,\Omega)=(\log |x|,x/|x|)\in\mathbb R\times S^3$. Let $\mathcal H(S^3)$ be the resulting graded Hilbert space, $E$ its dimensionless radial Hamiltonian, $J_1$ one chosen Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan generator, $F$ fermion parity, and $Q$ the selected supercharge with radial Hilbert adjoint $S=Q^\dagger$. In this normalization the superconformal algebra gives the nonnegative operator

$$\delta=2\{S,Q\}=E-2J_1-\frac32R.$$

Use the convention in which $Q$ is the component whose scalar chiral-primary branch has $d_{\mathcal O}-3r_{\mathcal O}/2$ as its anticommutator eigenvalue. For its conjugate component $\bar Q$ with radial adjoint $\bar S=\bar Q^\dagger$, write $J_2$ for the other Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan; its conjugate anticommutator is $2\{\bar S,\bar Q\}=E-2J_2+3R/2$. On a scalar superconformal primary both Cartan eigenvalues are zero, so these are the two scalar-primary positivity bounds used on this page.

derivations.claim: Using $S|\mathcal O\rangle=0$ and the Hilbert-adjoint relation, [F1] gives $(d_{\mathcal O}-\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O})\|\mathcal O\|^2=\langle\mathcal O|2\{S,Q\}|\mathcal O\rangle=2\|Q\mathcal O\|^2\geq0$. Thus $d_{\mathcal O}\geq\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O}$, with equality exactly when $Q|\mathcal O\rangle=0$.

The conjugate anticommutator similarly gives $(d_{\mathcal O}+\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O})\|\mathcal O\|^2=\langle\mathcal O|2\{\bar S,\bar Q\}|\mathcal O\rangle=2\|\bar Q\mathcal O\|^2\geq0$. Combining the two inequalities gives $d_{\mathcal O}\geq\max(\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O},-\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O})=\tfrac32|r_{\mathcal O}|$; the active equality condition is the first norm when $r_{\mathcal O}\geq0$ and the conjugate norm when $r_{\mathcal O}\leq0$.

citations.quote: An electric Wilson line is parallel transport traced in a representation of the global gauge group; a magnetic 't Hooft line is specified by a magnetic singularity around the support curve; a dyonic line carries both charges. Their center-charge classes are $(e,m)\in\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$. An allowed center-charge set is a subgroup $L\subseteq\mathcal C$ on which the displayed pairing vanishes; the three maximal such subgroups are the line-spectrum data for $SU(2)$, $SO(3)_+$, and $SO(3)_-$. The source-reported charge maps are $S:(e,m)\mapsto(m,-e)$ and $T:(e,m)\mapsto(e+m,m)$, so these transformations may change the global form. Kapustin and Witten's 2007 source explicitly describes quantum $S$-duality as a conjecture; Aharony, Seiberg, and Tachikawa's 2013 article gives the source-reported line spectra and charge transformations, including their global-form distinctions. This dated source status is recorded without an exhaustive literature-status review, an open-problem classification, or a proof of equivalence between the theories.

derivations.claim: The three nonzero elements of $\mathcal C$ are $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(1,1)$. Each generates an order-two subgroup with the origin. The pairing is alternating, so each such subgroup is isotropic. Any subgroup containing two distinct nonzero elements contains two linearly independent columns in $\mathbb Z_2^2$; the determinant $em'-me'$ of two independent columns is nonzero and therefore equals $1$ in $\mathbb Z_2$. Hence such a subgroup is not isotropic. Therefore these are exactly the three maximal isotropic subgroups, and [F2] gives their source-reported gauge-group labels.

Modulo $2$, the map $S$ sends $(1,0)$ to $(0,1)$, $(0,1)$ to $(1,0)$, and $(1,1)$ to $(1,1)$. The map $T$ sends $(1,0)$ to $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$ to $(1,1)$, and $(1,1)$ to $(0,1)$. These invertible linear maps therefore send the displayed subgroups exactly as stated. At fixed $g$, replacing $\theta$ by $\theta+2\pi$ adds $1$ to $\tau$ by [F1]. Source [F2] identifies this $T$ operation as a classical symmetry on $\mathbb R^4$, with the stated permutation of line-spectrum choices, and describes the additional quantum $S$-equivalence as conjectural. That $S$-equivalence is not established by the finite arithmetic.

Use the physical action brackets $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$ and $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from Physical superspace action brackets and canonical chiral components, with raw mathematical coefficient integrals $I_D,I_F$ unchanged. Physical chiral components obey $\psi_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sqrt2\psi$ and $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$. All physical action and coupling formulas below use these brackets and physical component names; adding Hermitian conjugation applies only to the F action and occurs once.

Use the oriented, time-oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb{R}^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^\mu$ of length, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, time orientation of increasing $x^0$, and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Let $P\to M$ be one smooth right-principal $SU(2)$ bundle, meaning its smooth right $SU(2)$ action is free and transitive on each fibre, it admits equivariant local trivializations, and its sector $[P]$ is the nonempty minimum-rank set code of its smooth equivariant bundle-isomorphism type over $M$, in the supplied non-Abelian gauge-data convention. The global group is $SU(2):=\{u\in M_2(\mathbb C):u^\dagger u=I_2,\det u=1\}$, not $SO(3)$; its Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{su}(2):=\{X\in M_2(\mathbb C):X^\dagger=-X,\operatorname{Tr}_2X=0\}$ and its adjoint action is $\operatorname{Ad}_uX=uXu^{-1}$. The Pauli matrices are $\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Use $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ with $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$, $c=\hbar=1$, and dimensionless coupling $g=g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. Use $\sigma^0=I_2$, $\sigma^j:=\sigma_j$ for these spatial matrices, $\bar\sigma^0=I_2$, $\bar\sigma^j=-\sigma^j$, and $\epsilon_{12}=1$, so $\sigma^\mu\bar\sigma^\nu+\sigma^\nu\bar\sigma^\mu=-2\eta^{\mu\nu}I_2$. Define the real adjoint bundle $\operatorname{ad}(P):=(P\times\mathfrak{su}(2))/\sim$ and its complexification $\operatorname{ad}(P)_{\mathbb C}:=(P\times\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C})/\sim$, both with relation $[pu,X]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_uX]$; the bar on $\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}$ is conjugation fixing $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. In the N=1 decomposition, $V_{\mathrm{ad}}$ is the dimensionless real adjoint vector prepotential with $e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}\mapsto e^{i\Lambda^\dagger}e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}e^{-i\Lambda}$, where $\Lambda$ is a chiral gauge-parameter superfield, and $\Phi_1,\Phi_2,\Phi_3$ are adjoint chiral superfields in connection normalization. Each $\Phi_i$ obeys $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi_i=0$ and has one complex adjoint scalar, one adjoint Weyl fermion, and an algebraic auxiliary field. In the fixed physical chiral expansion write its scalar component as $\phi_i$, a smooth section of $\operatorname{ad}(P)_{\mathbb C}$ with local representatives $\phi_{r,\alpha}:U_\alpha\to\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}$ obeying $\phi_{r,\beta}=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}}\phi_{r,\alpha}$ when local sections satisfy $s_\beta=s_\alpha g_{\alpha\beta}$. Define for $r=1,2,3$, with $\mathrm{i}^2=-1$

$$X^{2r-1}:=\frac{\phi_r+\overline{\phi_r}}{\sqrt2},\qquad X^{2r}:=\frac{\phi_r-\overline{\phi_r}}{\mathrm{i}\sqrt2},\qquad \phi_r=\frac{X^{2r-1}+\mathrm{i}X^{2r}}{\sqrt2}.$$

Thus each $X^I$ is a smooth section of $\operatorname{ad}(P)$, with local components transforming by $X^I_\beta=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}}X^I_\alpha$. The canonical chiral and real scalar fields are $\Phi_{i,\mathrm{can}}=\Phi_i/g$ and $X^I_{\mathrm{can}}=X^I/g$, respectively.


Write $\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}=\mathfrak{su}(2)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, let $\kappa_{\mathbb C}$ be the complex-bilinear extension of $\kappa$, set $\kappa_H(\bar X,Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\bar X,Y)$, and write $[X,Y]$ for the complexified Lie bracket. The complexified form is nondegenerate and adjoint-invariant. For $U=e^{i\Lambda}$, each adjoint chiral field transforms by $\Phi_i\mapsto U\Phi_iU^{-1}$, so the adjoint cubic in the action is gauge invariant under this law. Use $D_\alpha=\partial^L_{\theta^\alpha}+i\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}\bar\theta^{\dot\beta}\partial_\mu$ and $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}-i\theta^\beta\sigma^\mu_{\beta\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu$. Each $\Phi_i$ is an even chiral superfield satisfying $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi_i=0$, and the represented adjoint matrix curvature is $\mathscr C_{\alpha,\mathrm{ad}}=-\tfrac14\bar D^{\dot\beta}\bar D_{\dot\beta}(e^{-2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}D_\alpha e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}})$. The abstract connection-normalized chiral curvature in the action is $\mathcal W_\alpha$, defined by $\rho_{R*}(\mathcal W_\alpha)=\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}/(2i)$ for every representation $R$. Thus $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)/(4g^2)=\operatorname{Tr}_2(\mathscr C^\alpha\mathscr C_\alpha)/(8g^2)$ in the defining representation, before adding its Hermitian conjugate. The adopted connection-normalized N=1 action is

$$\mathcal L_{N=4}=\frac{1}{g^2}\left\{\frac14\left([\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)+\sum_{i=1}^3[\kappa_H(\bar\Phi_i,e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}\Phi_i)]_D+\left([\sqrt2\,\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\Phi_1,[\Phi_2,\Phi_3])]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)\right\}.$$

Here $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ and $[Z]_D=-I_D(Z)/4$ are the normalized physical brackets; the raw mathematical measures retain their coefficient-extraction meaning. In canonical fields, the cubic superpotential coefficient is $\sqrt2g$, so its Yukawa coupling equals the gauge coupling. On shell, meaning after eliminating algebraic auxiliary fields and imposing the field equations, the physical content is one gauge connection, six real adjoint scalars $X^I$ ($I=1,\ldots,6$), and four adjoint Weyl fermions $\lambda^A$ ($A=1,\ldots,4$). The scalar potential in connection normalization is

$$V_{\mathrm{scalar}}=\frac{1}{2g^2}\sum_{1\le I<J\le6}\kappa([X^I,X^J],[X^I,X^J]);$$

for canonical fields $X^I_{\mathrm{can}}=X^I/g$ this is $\frac{g^2}{2}\sum_{I<J}\kappa([X^I_{\mathrm{can}},X^J_{\mathrm{can}}],[X^I_{\mathrm{can}},X^J_{\mathrm{can}}])$. With the N=2 model's N=1 decomposition, this is the $R=\mathrm{ad}$, $m=0$ hypermultiplet specialization after rescaling its two canonical hypermultiplet chiral fields by $g$ to the connection normalization of $\Phi_2$ and $\Phi_3$.

Adopt rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ supersymmetry, with four independent left-Weyl supercharges and sixteen real components, as part of this physical model postulate. The action's extended invariance and on-shell closure are not proved in this item. This is a classical action with smooth fields in local bundle trivializations and compactly supported admissible variations; no path-integral measure, regulator, quantum continuum theory, or empirical result is asserted. Use $c=\hbar=1$: $g$ is dimensionless, connection-normalized scalar fields have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and canonical fields have mass dimension one.

For the scalar-primary sector, use the selected $\mathcal N=1$ subalgebra and normalize its $U(1)_R$ generator $R$ so that the three adjoint chiral superfields have scalar charge $2/3$. Write $d_{\mathcal O}$ for the eigenvalue of the dilation generator on a scalar superconformal primary $|\mathcal O\rangle$ and $r_{\mathcal O}$ for its $R$ charge. The scalar unitarity bound in this convention is $d_{\mathcal O}\geq 3|r_{\mathcal O}|/2$; equality in the positive-charge branch is the chiral-primary shortening condition. The local conditional norm argument is given by the chiral-primary unitarity item on this page; no classification of all $\mathfrak{psu}(2,2|4)$ representations is asserted here.

Let $\mathcal H$ be a Hilbert-space representation of the selected $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal subalgebra, with positive inner product and common invariant domain on which the radial adjoint relations in the definition hold. Let $|\mathcal O\rangle\neq0$ be a scalar superconformal primary with dilation eigenvalue $d_{\mathcal O}$ and $U(1)_R$ eigenvalue $r_{\mathcal O}$. Then

$$d_{\mathcal O}\geq\frac32|r_{\mathcal O}|.$$

If $r_{\mathcal O}\geq0$, equality holds exactly when the selected chiral-branch supercharge $Q$ annihilates $|\mathcal O\rangle$. If $r_{\mathcal O}\leq0$, equality holds exactly when its conjugate $\bar Q$ annihilates $|\mathcal O\rangle$. This is a conditional algebraic statement about a state already present in the assumed unitary representation; it does not construct that representation or a continuum SCFT.

derivations.claim: For a gauge transformation $U\in SU(2)$, $(UZU^{-1})^2=UZ^2U^{-1}$. For finite matrices, $\operatorname{Tr}_2(AB)=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}B_{ji}=\sum_{i,j}B_{ji}A_{ij}=\operatorname{Tr}_2(BA)$, so $\operatorname{Tr}_2(UZ^2U^{-1})=\operatorname{Tr}_2(Z^2U^{-1}U)=\operatorname{Tr}_2(Z^2)$. Under an $R$ rotation by $\alpha$, $Z\mapsto e^{2i\alpha/3}Z$, hence $Z^2\mapsto e^{4i\alpha/3}Z^2$ and the linear trace has charge $4/3$.

By step 1.1, the state has $r_{\mathcal O}=4/3>0$. The positive-branch hypothesis in [F3] therefore applies to the nonzero primary in [A1], giving $d_{\mathcal O}=\frac32\cdot\frac43=2$. This is a conditional representation-theoretic deduction; the engineering dimension of the classical composite is not being used as a substitute for the scaling-dimension proof.

For the superconformal index, use Euclidean radial quantization on a unit three-sphere, defined by writing the punctured Euclidean space as $(t,\Omega)=(\log |x|,x/|x|)\in\mathbb R\times S^3$. Let $\mathcal H(S^3)$ be the resulting graded Hilbert space, $E$ its dimensionless radial Hamiltonian, $J_1$ one chosen Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan generator, $F$ fermion parity, and $Q$ the selected supercharge with radial Hilbert adjoint $S=Q^\dagger$. In this normalization the superconformal algebra gives the nonnegative operator

$$\delta=2\{S,Q\}=E-2J_1-\frac32R.$$

Use the convention in which $Q$ is the component whose scalar chiral-primary branch has $d_{\mathcal O}-3r_{\mathcal O}/2$ as its anticommutator eigenvalue. For its conjugate component $\bar Q$ with radial adjoint $\bar S=\bar Q^\dagger$, write $J_2$ for the other Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan; its conjugate anticommutator is $2\{\bar S,\bar Q\}=E-2J_2+3R/2$. On a scalar superconformal primary both Cartan eigenvalues are zero, so these are the two scalar-primary positivity bounds used on this page.

For the index sector require the closed odd operator $D_Q=\sqrt2(Q+S)$ to be self-adjoint with $D_Q^2=\delta$ as a closed composition equality. Require also $\delta=2(SQ+QS)$ as an equality on the full intersection of the two composition domains, not merely as an extension of an identity on test vectors. Supply an orthonormal basis of simultaneous eigenvectors of $\delta,J_1',\ldots,J_k'$ and $(-1)^F$, with real energy/charge labels $(\lambda,\mathbf j)$, parity label $\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$, and maximal diagonal self-adjoint domains. The joint $(\lambda,\mathbf j)$ subspace includes the basis vectors of both parity labels; write $P_{\lambda,\mathbf j}$ for its orthogonal projection. Here $\lambda\ge0$, the joint energy/charge labels form a supplied countable set, and entire gap eigenspaces, including the protected kernel, may be infinite-dimensional. Require $P_{\lambda,\mathbf j}D(T)\subset D(T)$ and $TP_{\lambda,\mathbf j}\psi=P_{\lambda,\mathbf j}T\psi$ for $T=Q,S,D_Q$ on $D(T)$. These combined-parity projections are the reducing projections; parity-specific projections are not required to commute with odd operators. The grading preserves each joint $(\lambda,\mathbf j)$ subspace and anticommutes with the odd operators on their domains. These reducing-domain conditions specify the actual spectral compatibility; common-domain commutators alone are insufficient.

For $\beta>0$ and finite real or complex chemical potentials $\boldsymbol\mu$, define the weighted exponential first on the finite joint-eigenvector span by the eigenvalues $\exp(-\beta\lambda+\sum_a\mu_a j_a)$. Require its closure to be bounded trace class for every $\beta>0$ at the chosen $\boldsymbol\mu$. This is the meaning of the exponential in the index observable, not an unspecified product of unbounded operators. Every joint block then has finite dimension: its weight is nonzero and infinitely many equal singular values would violate trace class. Infinite total gap multiplicities are permitted through infinitely many joint blocks. Define

$$\mathcal I(\beta,\boldsymbol\mu)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H(S^3)}\left((-1)^F\exp\left[-\beta\delta+\sum_{a=1}^k\mu_aJ_a'\right]\right).$$

If the trace is not trace class, the same symbol may be used only for a specified formal series whose coefficients are defined; it does not denote a convergent partition function. The index is called protected against $\beta$-variation when the stated operator and trace hypotheses imply that positive-$\delta$ states cancel in the graded trace, as proved by the index-pair theorem on this page. A source's further claim of invariance under changing a coupling requires its own stated deformation hypotheses. A protected primary here means a named primary whose dimension is fixed by a specified shortening relation; the word alone asserts no deformation invariance.

derivations.claim: From $Q|b\rangle=\sqrt{\lambda/2}|f\rangle$, $Q|f\rangle=0$, and $S=Q^\dagger$, we have $SQ|b\rangle=(\lambda/2)|b\rangle$, $QS|b\rangle=0$, $SQ|f\rangle=0$, and $QS|f\rangle=(\lambda/2)|f\rangle$. Hence $\delta|b\rangle=\lambda|b\rangle$ and $\delta|f\rangle=\lambda|f\rangle$, so the kernel is zero.

The even state contributes $e^{-\beta\lambda}$ to the graded trace and the odd state contributes $-e^{-\beta\lambda}$. Their sum is zero for every $\beta>0$, and it equals the zero trace on the zero-dimensional kernel.
